title: Fix Stray Fragmented Lines Around Laser Engraving
body_html:
Stray Fragmented Lines Appear Around Engraved Graphics - VertiGO Series

When random, scattered lines or small artifacts appear around the perimeter of an engraved design, it can ruin an otherwise perfect project. Because the original file looks clean and may even process flawlessly on other machines, this issue points to a localized hardware vibration or data transfer error. This guide walks you through stabilizing your optical path and fixing data corruption to restore crisp, clean engraving edges.

Problem Description

Small, scattered, fragmented short lines appear around the perimeter of the engraved design that are completely absent from the original project file. Processing the exact same file on other laser machines yields perfect results with no artifacts.

Cause

  • The processing file data package becomes corrupted or suffers from package loss while being sent to the laser motherboard.
  • One or more lenses or mirrors along the optical path are loose, vibrating under the physical inertial forces of the laser head's movement and throwing off the beam trajectory.

Solution

Step 1. Modify the File Transfer Method or Connection Protocol

1. If you typically click "Start" directly inside your laser software to process jobs on the fly, data packet loss can occur during transmitting. Instead, click "Send" to upload the entire project file directly into the laser controller's onboard memory first. Once the transfer is complete, press "Start" on the machine's physical control panel to run the job locally.

2. You could try changing your connection method, as your current connection might be affected by something, such as external electromagnetic interference.

  • USB Connection
  • Ethernet Connection
  • Wi-Fi Connection

Step 2. Inspect the Entire Optical Path for Loose Optics

Starting directly from where the laser beam exits the RF tube, check the following components for any physical play or looseness: Beam Expander, 1st Mirror, Beam Combiner, 2nd Mirror, 3rd Mirror, and the Focus Lens.

If any lens or mirror is loose within its retaining housing, the rapid acceleration and deceleration of the laser head during engraving will cause that optic to shake. As the laser beam passes through a vibrating optic, its exit angle shifts dynamically, striking the material incorrectly and creating unintended stray lines.

 

Important Reminder:

If these steps do not resolve the issue, please submit a support ticket on ZOHO: https://zohodesk.1laser.com/portal/en/newticket. A technician will then be able to conduct a more in-depth diagnosis and resolve your problem.
